title: Don't crash on two kinds of malformed table
description:
Two malformed tables make `gridTable` throw instead of failing or parsing:

- a part separator without its closing `+`, e.g. a header line `+====` (`+---+` / `| a |` / `+====` / `| b |` / `+---+`): "Error in array index", from `findEnd` reading past the end of the line;
- a line ending in zero-width characters, e.g. an unterminated row ending in a combining accent: "(Array.!): undefined array element", because that row of the character grid was short.

This adds the bounds checks and the missing padding, and keeps the placeholder `'\0'` of such a character out of the cell content. Both cases have a test. I found them by mutating generated tables; with the fix, 50,000 mutated tables parse without an exception.
